title: module.yaml manifest
description: Every module — skill, agent, connector, gate, or wrapped legacy tool — ships this manifest regardless of what's inside it. See architecture plan §03.

phase.description: Which phase in phase-graph.yaml this module fills a capability slot in. Omit together with capability for a shared module — a standing capability (e.g. a client's own stack-specific agent) available in every session, not bound to any one phase's gate.

capability.description: The abstract slot this module fills, referenced from registry.yaml. Omit together with phase for a shared module.

description.description: Free-text description, used in the compiled agent/rule frontmatter when there's no phase/capability to derive one from. Mainly relevant for shared modules.

model_tier.description: Cost lever — route mechanical modules cheap, judgment-heavy modules to the top tier. See architecture plan §09.

owner.description: Team or channel accountable for this module

source_of_truth.description: Which external system wins on conflict, e.g. jira

hooks.description: Explicit tool->event bindings for scripts in hooks/. Claude Code and Cursor use different event names/granularity (PreToolUse+matcher vs. beforeShellExecution, etc.) so the binding is declared here rather than inferred from a filename.

script.description: Filename under this module's hooks/ directory

claude_matcher.description: e.g. Bash, Edit|Write — required if claude_event is set

cursor_fail_closed.description: Cursor's failClosed for this hook: true means a crash/timeout in the script BLOCKS the action. Only set it on hooks that are fail-closed by design (deploy-gate); a fail-open enforcement nudge (unit-test-writer) must leave it false, or a bug in the script blocks every shell command in Cursor.

always_apply.description: Compiled to Cursor's alwaysApply: true — the rule is always active regardless of the model's relevance judgment on the description. Use for policy-critical content (compliance, security) where 'probably gets auto-activated' isn't a strong enough guarantee. Most modules should leave this false and rely on a specific description instead.
